# Trailhead

> Trailhead is a headless task engine that humans and AI agents share. It stores projects and tasks and enforces the rules around them: claims with expiring leases, a ready queue, typed comments for handoffs and questions, dependencies, review, and an event log where every write can be undone. There is no app; every interface is a client of the REST API under `/v1`, the MCP server at `/mcp`, or the `trailhead` CLI.

Requests and responses are JSON. Tasks are named by key (`AUTH-42`) or UUID, projects by key (`AUTH`) or UUID. Timestamps are UTC RFC 3339. Deadlines and scheduling both take a day with an optional time: `due_on`/`due_at`/`due_tz` for when it's due, `scheduled_on`/`scheduled_at`/`scheduled_tz` for when it's planned to be worked. The `_on` field is a plain date (`2026-10-17`), `_at` an optional RFC 3339 time on it, `_tz` an IANA zone. A time sets the day to its date in the zone (or at the timestamp's own offset), so `_on` can be left out. A day-only deadline is due by the end of that day in `due_tz` (UTC without one), so `due_tz` may come without `due_at`; `scheduled_tz` needs `scheduled_at`. Priority is 1 (urgent) to 4 (low), default 3. A local server listens on `http://127.0.0.1:7241`.

## Auth

- Send `Authorization: Bearer th_...` on everything except `GET /v1/health`, `GET /v1/openapi.json` and `GET /llms.txt`. `GET /v1/me` says who you are.
- A token belongs to a user (a human) or an agent. Every agent acts for exactly one user, and every write records both. Agents never use a human's token.
- `POST /v1/agents` creates an agent and its first token together: if the token is refused, there is no agent. Agents can create sub-agents (`POST /v1/agents {"name"}` as an agent makes `<agent>/<name>`) and issue them tokens that never exceed their own projects or rate limit; `POST /v1/agents/{agent}/revoke` revokes an agent and everything under it. Over MCP, `register_agent` then `as_agent` on any tool lets one connection act as several registered sub-agents.
- Agents can't revert, issue tokens for anyone but their sub-agents, or approve review (unless a project lists them as `reviewers`). Humans can edit, release or finish a task another actor holds; agents can't.
- A token may be scoped to projects. Anything outside the scope reads as `not_found`; writes naming an out-of-scope project are `forbidden`. A blocker outside the scope shows as `(out of scope)`.
- A token may expire: `expires_in_seconds` when issuing it (`POST /v1/tokens`, `POST /v1/agents`). An expired token gets `401`. A token never outlives the one that issued it: without `expires_in_seconds` it inherits the issuer's expiry, and asking for longer is `forbidden`.
- A token may have a per-minute rate limit. Over it: `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After` seconds and `retry_after` in the body.
- A human can change a token's scope or limit without reissuing it: `PATCH /v1/tokens/{id} {"projects": ["AUTH"], "rate_limit_per_minute": 60}`; omit a field to keep it, `null` to lift it.
- A token names the apps whose data it reaches (`"apps": ["cairn"]` when issuing it or in `PATCH /v1/tokens/{id}`, never more than the issuer's). One that names none reaches no app's data if it is an agent's, every app if it is a person's not limited to projects; `null` in a `PATCH` goes back to that default. A sub-agent's token reaches none unless given some.

## Core loop

1. `GET /v1/ready?project=KEY&limit=N` lists open, unclaimed, unblocked tasks in active projects, by priority, then due date, then age. Default limit 20.
2. Read the project brief (`GET /v1/projects/KEY`, field `brief`): goals, conventions, definition of done.
3. `POST /v1/tasks/KEY-1/claim` with optional `{"ttl": seconds}` (1 to 86400; default the project's `claim_ttl`, else the workspace's, normally 1800). Moves the task to `in_progress` and returns `{task, claim, handoff}`, where `handoff` is the last handoff comment left on it. Read it. Claiming a task you already hold extends the lease. Only an `open` task can be claimed. A human's claim without a `ttl` never expires (`expires_at` is `null`): leases exist so a crashed agent's work comes back, and a person can release a forgotten claim by hand.
4. Renew about every third of the TTL: `POST /v1/tasks/KEY-1/renew` (optional `{"ttl"}`). An expired claim is dropped and an `in_progress` task goes back to `open`. `409 claim_lost` on renew means your lease expired or someone else took the task: stop, re-read the task, and claim it again if it is still yours to do. Renewing a claim that never expires, without a `ttl`, changes nothing. `GET /v1/claims` lists the claims you hold.
5. Comment as you go: `POST /v1/tasks/KEY-1/comments` with `{"kind", "body", "addressed_to"?}`.
6. Finish: `PATCH /v1/tasks/KEY-1` with `{"status": "done", "handoff": "..."}` (or `in_review`), the handoff saying what changed, what's left and any gotchas. Both are written together or, if the status is refused, neither. Either status releases the claim. To stop without finishing, leave a handoff and `POST /v1/tasks/KEY-1/release`, which returns the task to `open`.

## Comments

`kind` is one of:

- `handoff`: what was done, what's left, gotchas. The latest one comes back with the next claim.
- `progress`: short status updates.
- `question`: needs an answer, from a human or another agent (`addressed_to` takes a user or agent id). Moves the task to `needs_input`, out of the ready queue. `POST /v1/comments/{id}/resolve` with optional `{"answer"}` resolves it; the answer is posted as a `note` to the asker. When the last open question resolves, the task returns to `in_progress` if still claimed, else `open`. A person can instead set a parked task aside: `POST /v1/tasks/KEY-1/set-aside` with optional `{"note"}` resolves its open questions with a note saying so, clears its grade and moves it to `open` (dropping any claim), in one write; the factory leaves an ungraded task alone until a person grades it again. Agents get 403, and a task `in_progress` (a run may be going) is refused.
- `decision`: a choice and why, so later agents don't relitigate it.
- `review`: a verdict on a change. Needs `verdict` (`approve` or `request_changes`) and may name the reviewing `model`. It records the verdict only; moving the task is a separate step.
- `note`: anything else. The default.

The `description` is the current spec and gets edited; comments are the append-only history.

## Notifications

What a person is told. The server raises one by rule (an agent's question that isn't put to another agent, a task sent for review where no agent may approve, a task due soon or overdue) and resolves it when the thing is dealt with. To ask a person something, ask a `question`; raise one yourself only for what no rule covers.

- `POST /v1/notifications` with `{source, kind, title, body?, subject?, task?, actions?}` raises one. `source` names the raiser and `kind` the sort of thing, each 1 to 64 characters; `title` is one line; `subject` is your name for what it is about; `task` is a key, and finishing that task resolves it; `actions` are up to 4 `{label, url}` web links.
- `GET /v1/notifications?unread=&before=&limit=` returns `{notifications, unread}`, newest first.
- `POST /v1/notifications/{id}/resolve`, or `POST /v1/notifications/resolve` with `{source, subject}`, says the thing no longer needs the person. Marking one read (`/read`, `/unread`, `/read-all`) is the person's alone.
- Each change is an event (`notification.raised`, `.read`, `.unread`, `.resolved`) on the stream; undo leaves them alone.

## Pictures

A task can carry pictures, such as screenshots of a UI before and after a change. Whoever may comment on a task may attach one.

- `POST /v1/tasks/KEY-1/attachments?name=&role=&set=` with the PNG's bytes as the body and `Content-Type: image/png`. `name` (required) is 1 to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, such as `ticklist-today-dark`; a before and an after of one view share it. `role` is `before` or `after`; `set` (up to 64 characters) groups pictures taken together, such as a run id or a commit. Only PNGs (checked by their bytes) of at most 2 MiB; a task holds at most 64, and 32 MiB together. Answers `201` with the attachment's metadata: `{id, task_id, name, content_type, size, sha256, width, height, role?, set?, created_by, on_behalf_of, created_at, deleted_at}`.
- `GET /v1/tasks/KEY-1/attachments` lists them, oldest first, without bytes; `GET /v1/tasks?include=attachments` adds the same list to each task, and `GET /v1/tasks/KEY-1` carries it as `attachments`.
- `GET /v1/attachments/{id}` returns the bytes, with `ETag` (the SHA-256) and an immutable `Cache-Control`; `If-None-Match` gets `304`.
- `DELETE /v1/attachments/{id}` removes one (undo restores it). A person may remove any; an agent only those it or its sub-agents added (`403` otherwise).

## App data

Each app in the window keeps its own records, in collections its `collections.toml` declares (`[collections.snoozes]` with `fields = { item = "string", until = "timestamp?" }`): a field is `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `timestamp` (RFC 3339), `day` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `url` or `json`, `[]` after it for a list, then `?` for optional. A write with a field missing, unknown or of the wrong type is `400 invalid` naming the field; an optional field sent as `null` is the same as left out. A collection with `from = "<connector>.<feed>"` is filled from a connector's feed and is read-only here (`403 forbidden`). `{app}` is the app's id, such as `cairn`. A token that doesn't reach the app gets `403` on all of these.

- `GET /v1/apps` lists the apps with data you reach, each `{id, collections}`; `GET /v1/apps/{app}` is one. `PUT /v1/apps/{app}/declaration` (a person only) registers an app's `collections.toml`, sent as text, or as its JSON form with `Content-Type: application/json`; the server also registers them itself from the apps repo it builds. A collection that holds records changes only by addition (a new collection or a new optional field).
- A record is `{id, collection, key, data, version, created_at, updated_at, created_by}`. `key` is optional: the name something outside gave it (`lanesawyer/trailhead#123`), unique in its collection.
- `GET /v1/apps/{app}/records/{collection}?after=<id>&limit=` pages records in the order they were made (default 100, at most 1000). The `trailhead-event-cursor` header is the app's newest event as the page was read.
- `POST /v1/apps/{app}/records/{collection}` with `{"data", "key"?}` creates one (`201`; a taken key is `409 already_exists`). `GET`, `PATCH` (a JSON merge patch of `data`), `PUT` (the whole `data`; the key stays) and `DELETE` `/v1/apps/{app}/records/{collection}/{id}`. Reads return `ETag: "<version>"`; send it as `If-Match` on `PATCH`, `PUT` or `DELETE`, and a stale one is `412 version_conflict`. `PATCH` and `PUT` answer `{outcome, record}`, `outcome` being `changed`, or `unchanged` when the record already looked like that (nothing written, no event, same version).
- `PUT /v1/apps/{app}/keys/{collection}/{key}` with the record's `data` writes by key: `201` `created`, or `200` `changed` or `unchanged`, so writing the same thing twice leaves one record and one event. The key is one percent-encoded path segment: `/` is `%2F`, `#` is `%23`. `GET` the same path reads it.
- `POST /v1/apps/{app}/batch` with `{"writes": [...]}` applies 1 to 1000 writes in one transaction, all or none: each `{"op": "create", collection, key?, data}`, `{"op": "patch", id, data, version?}`, `{"op": "replace", id, data, version?}`, `{"op": "delete", id, version?}` or `{"op": "put", collection, key, data}`. It answers `{batch_id, results}`, each result an `{outcome, record}`.
- Every change is an event in the app's own log, numbered per app: `{id, batch_id, actor_id, on_behalf_of, collection, record_id, kind, before, after, undoes, at}`, `kind` being `record.created|updated|deleted|reverted`. `GET /v1/apps/{app}/events?after=&collection=&record=&limit=` lists them; `GET /v1/apps/{app}/events/stream?after=&collection=&record=` streams them as the task stream does (`Last-Event-ID` resumes). To mirror a collection, read its pages, then stream from the first page's `trailhead-event-cursor`: one page misses and repeats nothing, and across pages apply an event only when its `after.version` is newer than the record you hold.
- `POST /v1/apps/{app}/undo` with `{"event_id"}` or `{"batch_id"}` (the `trailhead-batch` header of the write) undoes it, as for tasks; a collection filled from a feed is left for its next run to set.

## Connectors

A connector is a small program in the apps repo (`connectors/<id>/`) that the server builds and runs on a schedule; each run hands over feeds of records, which the server writes into every app collection that says `from = "<id>.<feed>"`. Only a person reads or changes them here.

- `GET /v1/connectors` lists every connector the last build of the apps repo holds; `GET /v1/connectors/{id}` is one: `{id, name, error?, every_secs, timeout_secs, hosts, settings: [{name, kind, label, help?, required, value?}], secrets: [{name, set}], feeds: [{name, fields, collections}], enabled, missing, running, last_run?, next_run?}`. `missing` says in words what it needs before it can run (a setting, a secret, a build); `last_run` is `{started_at, duration_ms, ok, error?, feeds: {<feed>: {records, created, changed, removed, unchanged, errors?}}}`. A secret's value is never shown.
- `PATCH /v1/connectors/{id}` with `{"enabled"?, "settings"?}` turns it on or off and merges `settings` into what is set (`null` unsets one); a setting it doesn't declare, or of the wrong kind (`string`, `list`, `boolean`, `integer`), is `400 invalid`. Turning it on makes its agent, `connector/<id>`. Its secrets are given only on the server's machine: `trailhead connector login <id>`.
- `POST /v1/connectors/{id}/run` starts a run now and answers `202` once it has started (`409 already_exists` while one runs; `400 invalid` when it is off or still needs something).
- `PUT /v1/connectors/{id}/feeds/{feed}` with `{"records": [{"key", "data"}]}` is how a run hands a feed's whole current set over (at most 64 MB of JSON). Only the connector's own agent may (`403` for anyone else, a person too); its token reaches nothing else. A record that doesn't match the feed's fields is `400 invalid`, naming the feed, the key and the field. The answer is `{feed, records, apps: [{app, collection, created, changed, removed, unchanged, error?}]}`: one app failing stops none of the others, and a set that matches what an app holds writes nothing there.

## Statuses

`open`, `in_progress`, `needs_input`, `in_review`, `approved`, `done`, `cancelled`. Allowed moves (anything else is `409 invalid_transition` with `from` and `to`):

- `open` -> `in_progress`, `needs_input`, `in_review`, `done`, `cancelled`
- `in_progress` -> `open`, `needs_input`, `in_review`, `done`, `cancelled`
- `needs_input` -> `open`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`
- `in_review` -> `open`, `in_progress`, `needs_input`, `approved`, `done`, `cancelled`
- `approved` -> `open`, `in_review`, `done`, `cancelled`
- `done`, `cancelled` -> `open`

Moving to anything but `in_progress` or `needs_input` releases the claim.

## Review

A project with `require_review: true` won't let agents set `done`; send work to `in_review` instead. In every project, only a human (or a delegated reviewer, below) can move `in_review` to `approved` or `done`, or `approved` to `done`; other agents get `403 review_required` moving `in_review` on, and `403 forbidden` moving `approved` to `done`.

A project's `reviewers` (set by a human: `PATCH /v1/projects/KEY {"reviewers": ["agent-name"]}`) are agents allowed to approve like a human, except work they sent to review or held the last claim on before it went there; approving or finishing that work is `403 forbidden`, not `review_required`.

Agents can turn `require_review` on but not off, and can't archive or unarchive a project or change its `reviewers`, whether with `PATCH` or by undoing or reverting a human's change (`403 forbidden`).

## Dependencies

"Blocked" is computed, never stored: a task is blocked while any blocker is not `done` or `cancelled`. Blocked tasks stay out of `ready`, and claiming one is `409 blocked_by` with the blocker keys in `blocked_by`.

"Changes requested" is computed as well: an `in_review` task has it when its newest `review` comment with a verdict is `request_changes` and no `handoff` comment came after it. The task stays `in_review` (its PR is in the review loop) and the flag says it is the worker's move; claiming it works as for any `in_review` task, a handoff answers it, and releasing a rework returns it to `in_review`. `GET /v1/tasks/KEY` returns `changes_requested` (the verdict comment's id) when set, and `GET /v1/tasks?changes_requested=true` lists them.

- `POST /v1/tasks/KEY-2/blockers` `{"blocker": "KEY-1"}` makes KEY-1 block KEY-2. `GET` lists blockers; `DELETE /v1/tasks/KEY-2/blockers/KEY-1` removes one. Adding an existing dependency returns it unchanged; a cycle is `409 dependency_cycle`.
- `POST /v1/tasks` takes `blocked_by` and `blocks` arrays, added with the task: if one is refused (`404`, `409 dependency_cycle`), no task is created. To get help on your own task, create a subtask with `"blocks": ["KEY-1"]` and `"parent": "KEY-1"`; KEY-1 is ready again once the subtask is done.

## Tasks

- `POST /v1/tasks` `{"project", "title", "description"?, "priority"?, "grade"?, "due_on"?, "due_at"?, "due_tz"?, "scheduled_on"?, "scheduled_at"?, "scheduled_tz"?, "parent"?, "metadata"?, "blocked_by"?, "blocks"?, "source"?, "external_id"?}`. `source` and `external_id` go together; repeating a pair returns the existing task instead of a duplicate. The response carries `possible_duplicates` (keys of unfinished tasks in the project with a similar title) when there are any: a warning, not an error. Check them before carrying on. To look first, `GET /v1/tasks?title=...` (or `list_tasks` with `title`) returns tasks with exactly that title, ignoring case and surrounding space.
- `GET /v1/tasks?project=&status=a,b&parent=&due_before=&scheduled_through=&metadata=k:v,k2:v2&sort=&limit=&offset=` defaults to everything not done or cancelled. `grade=` takes `1` to `4`, `graded` or `ungraded` (`/v1/ready` takes it too). `changes_requested=true` keeps only `in_review` tasks waiting on a rework, `false` leaves them out. `scheduled_through=YYYY-MM-DD` keeps tasks scheduled on or before that day: today's date gives today's plan plus anything planned earlier and not finished. `sort` is `priority` (default: priority, then due date, then oldest), `updated_at` or `created_at`, with `-` for newest first, or `scheduled` (by scheduled day, timed tasks in time order before untimed ones, unscheduled last); page with `limit` (default 100) and `offset`. `include=` takes any of `claim` (the live claim or `null`, with the holder's name as `holder`), `open_questions` (unresolved questions, oldest first) `last_handoff` (the newest handoff or `null`) and `last_review` (the newest review with a verdict or `null`; with `last_handoff`, what changes requested is computed from), `blocked_by` and `attachments`, so an inbox of `status=needs_input,in_review` is one request.
- `grade` is an optional risk grade, 1 to 4. Only a human can create a task with one, lower it or clear it (`null`); an agent can only raise an existing grade, and undo or revert are held to the same rule.
- `GET /v1/tasks/KEY-1` returns `{task, claim, blocked_by, changes_requested?, blocks, comments, duplicate_of, duplicates, attachments}`.
- `PATCH /v1/tasks/KEY-1` takes any of `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`, `grade`, `duplicate_of`, `due_on`, `due_at`, `due_tz`, `scheduled_on`, `scheduled_at`, `scheduled_tz`, `parent`, `metadata` (a JSON merge patch: `null` removes a key), and `handoff`, a handoff comment written with the update or not at all. `null` clears any of the fields. For both deadlines and scheduling, a new `_on` day alone drops any time, a `null` `_at` keeps the day, and a `null` `_on` clears the time and zone too. `due_before` compares against when the deadline passes, so a day-only deadline counts as the end of its day.
- `duplicate_of` is the key of the task a cancelled task duplicates: send it with `"status": "cancelled"`. `GET /v1/tasks/KEY-1` then returns `duplicate_of` (a key) on it and `duplicates` (keys) on the original. `null` clears it, as does reopening the task.
- `DELETE /v1/tasks/KEY-1` soft-deletes; undo restores it.
- `GET /v1/search?q=&project=&status=a,b&limit=` searches titles, descriptions and comments, open work first. Each hit has `match`: `{field, snippet, comment_id}`, where `field` is the first of `title`, `description` or `comment` that matched and `snippet` is plain text around the match.

## Concurrency

Task and project reads return `ETag: "<version>"`; `version` increments on every write. Send it back as `If-Match: "<version>"` on `PATCH` or `DELETE` (or `"version"` in a task `PATCH` body). A stale version is `412 version_conflict` with `current_version`: re-read, reapply, retry. Without `If-Match` the write applies unconditionally.

## Idempotency

Any `/v1` write may send `Idempotency-Key` (1-255 characters). A retry with the same key and same request (method, path and query, body) replays the stored 2xx response with `idempotent-replayed: true` instead of running again. The same key on a different request is `422 idempotency_key_reused`; a retry while the first is still running is `409 idempotency_key_in_flight`. Failed requests aren't stored, so retry them with the same key. Keys belong to the token and last 24 hours.

## Undo

Every request is one batch; its id is in the `trailhead-batch` response header. `POST /v1/undo` with `{"batch_id"}` or `{"event_id"}` reverts it, as a new write that can itself be undone. If something it touched changed later it fails with `409 undo_conflict` (`later_event`); past 90 days it is `409 undo_window_expired`. A human can `POST /v1/revert` `{"actor_id", "since"}` to revert everything one actor did since a time, skipping and reporting anything someone else changed afterwards, or a task restore that would form a parent cycle (`later_event` null, cause in `reason`). It reverts the actor's writes to apps' data too, each app on its own after the tasks: `apps` reports each app it changed anything in by id, and `apps_failed` any app whose revert failed, with why; both are left out when empty.

## Events

Every write appends an event: `{id, batch_id, actor_id, on_behalf_of, task_id, task_key, entity, entity_id, kind, before, after, undoes, at}`. Kinds: `task.created|updated|deleted`, `claim.acquired|renewed|released|expired`, `comment.created|resolved`, `dependency.added|removed`, `project.created|updated`, `agent.created` (its `task_id` is null; scoped tokens and `project=` filters never see it, and `changes_only` hides it), `<entity>.reverted`, and the reminders `task.due_soon` (within 24 hours) and `task.overdue`.

- `GET /v1/events?after=ID&before=ID&task=&project=KEY&actor=&batch=&since=&limit=&newest_first=true&changes_only=true&kinds=claim.,comment.created` (`changes_only` hides reminders; `kinds` keeps events whose kind starts with one of the prefixes, applied before `limit`; page back through history with `newest_first=true&before=<last id>`). `GET /v1/tasks/KEY-1/history` is one task's log.
- `GET /v1/events/stream?task=&project=KEY&kinds=task.,comment.created` is Server-Sent Events: `id` is the event id, `event` the kind, `data` the event JSON. On reconnect send `Last-Event-ID` (or `?after=`) to resume with nothing missed. With neither, the stream starts after the newest event.

## Webhooks

Humans with unscoped tokens can register `POST /v1/webhooks {"url", "event_kinds": ["task.", ...]}` (empty kinds means every event); the response carries a `whsec_` signing secret, shown once. Each event is POSTed as its JSON with headers `trailhead-event-id`, `trailhead-event-kind`, `trailhead-webhook-id` and `trailhead-signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">` keyed by the secret; verify it and reject old timestamps. Delivery is ordered and at-least-once (dedupe on the event id). A non-2xx response stops the queue and retries with exponential backoff up to an hour; 20 failures in a row disable the webhook. `GET /v1/webhooks`, `DELETE /v1/webhooks/{id}`, and `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` for the attempt log. Except on the local server, targets must resolve to public addresses and redirects aren't followed; a private target fails like any other delivery and shows in the attempt log.

## Compact output

`GET /v1/tasks`, `/v1/ready` and `/v1/search` accept `?fields=key,title,status,version` to trim each task to those fields. Ask for only what you need.

## Errors

Every error is `{"error": {"code", "message", ...}}`. Branch on `code`, which is stable; `message` is for people. Codes and HTTP statuses:

- `invalid` 400: bad input; `message` says what.
- `unauthorized` 401: missing, invalid or revoked token.
- `forbidden` 403: not allowed for this caller or token scope.
- `review_required` 403: an agent tried to set `approved` or `done` on work that has to go through review first, or the agent isn't a delegated reviewer. `forbidden` instead: a delegated reviewer approving or finishing work it did itself, and any non-reviewer agent moving `approved` to `done`.
- `not_found` 404: no such thing, or outside your token's scope.
- `claim_held` 409: someone else holds the claim; `holder`, `holder_id`, `expires_at` (`null` if it never expires).
- `not_claim_holder` 409: you don't hold a claim on this task.
- `claim_lost` 409: on renew, your claim expired or someone else took the task; claim it again before continuing.
- `blocked_by` 409: unfinished blockers, listed in `blocked_by`.
- `invalid_transition` 409: that status move isn't allowed; `from`, `to`.
- `dependency_cycle` 409: the dependency would create a cycle.
- `undo_conflict` 409: something changed after the event; `later_event`.
- `undo_window_expired` 409: older than the 90-day undo window.
- `already_exists` 409: a project with that key exists, or a record with that key in its collection.
- `idempotency_key_in_flight` 409: a request with this key is still running; retry shortly.
- `version_conflict` 412: stale `If-Match` or `version`; `current_version`.
- `idempotency_key_reused` 422: this key was used for a different request.
- `rate_limited` 429: wait `Retry-After` seconds.
- `internal` 500: unexpected server error.

## More

- OpenAPI 3.1, every route and schema: `GET /v1/openapi.json`.
- MCP (streamable HTTP, same bearer tokens): `/mcp`. Tools `ready`, `list_tasks`, `show`, `create_task`, `update_task` (takes a `handoff`), `claim`, `renew`, `release`, `my_claims`, `comment`, `resolve_question`, `search`, `undo_last`, `list_projects`, `show_project`, `create_project`, `update_project` (name and brief only), and for apps' data, with a token that reaches the app: `app_collections`, `list_records`, `get_record`, `write_record` (create, change by `id`, or write by `key`) and `delete_record`. Each call is its own undo batch; errors come back as tool errors `error[code]: message`. Project briefs are resources at `trailhead://projects/KEY/brief`.
- CLI: `trailhead --as <agent> ready|claim|renew|comment|ask|done -m|release|mine|watch`. `trailhead --as <agent> mcp` bridges MCP over stdio.
